title: Hit-rate explainability and conservative cache policy composer
creator: Ava Nguyen
description:
Problem: We lack a reproducible, auditable way to explain KV/prefix cache hit-rate changes when applying automatic TTL and key-shaping recommendations. That makes safe automated applies risky: cost regressions can occur when batching and prefixing interact in non-linear ways, and engineers are left to guess rollback thresholds.

Goal: Build an explainability + conservative policy composer that (1) decomposes observed hit-rate changes into candidate causes (key design, request prefixes, sequence-length, batching window), (2) produces a conservative, confidence-aware cache policy proposal (per-prefix TTL bands + suggested key-normalization) and (3) provides an automated safe-apply pipeline with canary/shadow checks and deterministic rollback triggers.

Design summary:
- Hit-rate explainability engine: a lightweight Bayesian attribution model that returns per-prefix contributions and confidence intervals. It ingests sampled traces (prefix, sequence_len, batch_size, partial_hits) and outputs "attribution shards" that indicate how much of a delta is likely due to keying vs workload shift.
- Conservative policy composer: given hit attribution and cost model, produce a policy bundle with: suggested TTL ranges (min/median/max), sampling fraction for rollout, and a conservative batch-related modifier (reduce TTL gain if batching variance is high). Each recommendation includes a confidence score and an expected tokens-saved estimate.
- Safe apply pipeline: staged apply flow with the following phases: preview -> shadow -> canary (1%/5%/25% ramps) -> global apply. Safety gates: undesired cost delta (> +8%), hit-rate drop (> 5% relative), error rate increase (> 0.1 p95), tail-latency regressions. Failure of any gate triggers automated rollback and a generated incident report.

Telemetry & metrics:
- Required inputs: per-request prefix key, client_id (hashed), model, sequence_length, batch_size, token_count, result hash (for change-detection), timestamp.
- Outputs: per-prefix hit-rate baseline, post-change hit-rate, attribution breakdown, tokens-saved estimate, expected cost delta, recommendation confidence.

Rollout & testing plan:
1) Offline validation (2 weeks): run composer against historical telemetry and run counterfactual simulations to estimate false positive/negative rates.
2) Shadow pilot (1 week): apply recommendations in shadow mode for small set of clients (100 clients) and compare real vs shadow metrics.
3) Canary apply (2-day ramps): 1% -> 5% -> 25% traffic with automated checks at each step. If gates pass, continue to 100% over 24 hours.

Acceptance criteria:
- Composer produces recommendations for >= 90% of observed prefixes with a non-empty confidence score.
- At least 80% of recommendations that we applied in the shadow pilot show non-negative token savings in counterfactual simulation.
- Safe-apply pipeline triggers rollback automatically for injected failures in controlled experiments.

Notes & tradeoffs:
- We accept that the explainability model is probabilistic: to avoid aggressive cost-first moves we bias the composer toward conservative TTLs when confidence < 0.7.
- For multi-tenant prefixes, recommendations are namespaced by tenancy and may have tenant-specific lower TTL bounds to avoid noisy cross-tenant interference.
- We will avoid per-request heavy instrumentation; default sampling = 1% with adaptive up-sampling for new/volatile prefixes.

telemetry_queries: sample_prefix_aggregation: SELECT prefix, count(*) as rps, avg(sequence_len) FROM kv_requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY prefix LIMIT 500
hit_delta_monitor: SELECT prefix, baseline_hit, current_hit, (current_hit - baseline_hit)/baseline_hit as rel_delta FROM prefix_hit_metrics WHERE window = '1h' ORDER BY abs(rel_delta) DESC LIMIT 200
acceptance_criteria: Composer recommendations generated, shadow tests simulate non-negative cost for >=80% of applied recommendations, safe-apply rollbacks automatically when gates are violated, Console displays confidence and attribution per recommendation.
implementation_notes: Implement attribution as an online updater: maintain per-prefix Beta priors for hit probability adjusted by sequence_len and batch_size strata. Composer will prefer upward conservative rounding for TTL when confidence < 0.7. All policy bundles are versioned and immutable; apply flow must record commit SHA and telemetry snapshot.
